subject: PPSA annex: data provenance, flow ownership, and evidence request
messages:
From: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@medicore.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: MediCore Legal <gdpr@medicore.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: PPSA annex — provenance & ownership questions

Hi Hannah,

We're reviewing the PPSA draft you sent and have a couple of follow-ups focused on data provenance and ownership in the event logs and derivative artifacts. Specifically: 

1) Can you confirm which Redwood services are considered the authoritative source for event provenance (ingest timestamps, request IDs, model-version labels)? We need this for our audit trail.

2) For derived outputs (e.g., embeddings, reranks), who is the canonical owner of the artifact — MediCore (customer) or Redwood — for the purposes of our retention policy? The PPSA text is a bit ambiguous.

3) We also need a clear data flow diagram that shows transformation points where PII is tokenized, masked, or persisted. Will you be able to provide an updated diagram and a CSV mapping of PII fields to storage locations?

Can you share the artifacts by EOD Friday PST? We're aiming to close this during our internal compliance review.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Rourke
Senior Information Security Manager
MediCore Health

Attachments: none

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PPSA annex — provenance & ownership questions

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front, and we'll attach the artifacts in a follow-up from engineering: 

1) Authoritative provenance: Redwood's request ingestion service (ingest-api) records the canonical ingest timestamp and request_id. Model-serving adds model_version and node_metadata during runtime; both are surfaced to the audit log stream (immutable) which is the canonical audit trail.

2) Derived outputs: For the PPSA we treat customer input and derived artifacts as customer data; Redwood processes and stores transient copies required for caching/serving but the retention/owner semantics in Annex B indicate customer ownership of outputs unless otherwise agreed in the SOW. We'll highlight this language to avoid ambiguity.

3) We'll provide: (a) a data flow diagram showing transformation & persistence boundaries, (b) a CSV mapping PII fields to persistent stores and access tiers, and (c) an excerpt of the audit-log schema showing provenance fields.

Marissa is putting the diagram together; Priyom will scope the PII field mapping and retention rows. Connor, can you include the KMS key custody and rotation schedule for the PPSA exhibit?

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 4:12 PM Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@medicore.com> wrote:
> We're reviewing the PPSA draft and have a couple of follow-ups...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@medicore.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: PPSA artifacts: dataflow diagram + field mapping (draft)

Hi Liam — attaching the requested draft artifacts for your review. Notes below.

Attachments:
- dataflow_v1.svg (image/svg) — shows system boundaries, transformation points, and where tokenization/masking occurs.
- pii_field_mapping.csv (text/csv) — column: pii_field, example_path, retention_days, access_tier, storage_backend.

Key callouts from the diagram: 
- Tokenization/masking occurs at the ingestion gateway for customer-supplied PII when "tokenize_on_ingest" is enabled (configurable per tenant).
- Short-lived caches (default TTL 2 minutes) store KV cache for active sessions; cache data is not persisted to long-term storage unless explicitly saved by customer workflow.
- Embeddings & rerank artifacts are written to the customer dataset bucket (S3-compatible) by default and are labeled with request_id and model_version metadata in object metadata. That bucket is encrypted with a customer-scoped KMS key when requested (see KMS note).

We flagged a couple of items in the CSV where retention defaults could conflict with customer policies; please mark rows where you need custom retention or exclusions.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dataflow_v1.svg, pii_field_mapping.csv

From: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@medicore.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, MediCore Legal <gdpr@medicore.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PPSA artifacts: dataflow diagram + field mapping (draft)

Thanks Marissa — helpful diagrams. Two clarifying questions: 

A) KMS custody: the diagram notes customer-scoped KMS keys "when requested". Is BYOK/HSM supported for the Dedicated/Private options referenced in the PPSA, and do you have an attestation or schedule for key rotation we can include in our evidence pack?

B) Cross-border transient caches: are those caches ever geo-replicated for HA, and if so, how is customer PII excluded or scoped? We need to confirm that caches won't be replicated to our non-approved regions.

If you can point us to the KMS rotation doc and confirm the cache scoping behavior, we can mark the CSV rows and move forward.

-Liam

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@medicore.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PPSA artifacts: dataflow diagram + field mapping (draft)

Hi Liam — quick consolidated answers and links below.

A) KMS custody & BYOK: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed key import where required. Attached is the rotation schedule excerpt and attestation stub; we also published the formal KMS integration guide in our secure docs (link below). For PPSA evidence, use KMS-ROT-2026-09 as the rotation artifact id.

B) Cache geo-replication: Transient KV caches are region-scoped by default and are not geo-replicated across regions unless customer enables multi-region HA in the deployment config. For MediCore's PPSA we will mark the tenant config to disallow cross-region replication (single-region only). 

Links / artifacts: 
- KMS rotation schedule (attached): kms_key_rotation_schedule.pdf
- KMS integration guide: https://redwood.app/secure/ppsa/records/KMS-INTEGRATION-2026
- Draft dataflow folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-example-dataflow

Next steps: 
- Liam: mark pii_field_mapping.csv rows needing custom retention and confirm single-region enforcement.
- Marissa/Connor: we'll produce a short attestation (1–2 pages) referencing KMS-ROT-2026-09 and enclave custody notes.
- Hannah: can we align wording in Annex B to explicitly state: "Derived artifacts are treated as Customer Data; Redwood stores transient processing copies only for operational necessity, except where Customer requests persistent storage."

I'll follow up with the attestation stub later today.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms_key_rotation_schedule.pdf
